Subtitle: Connect your Teams status to Home Assistant
MenuAway: Home Assistant: paused (not in a home network)
UpdateBalloon: Teams Busy Light {0} is available. Click to open the release page.
WebhookHint: Shown in Home Assistant after adding the Teams Busy Light integration, later under Configure.
HeartbeatHint: Must be shorter than the offline timeout of the integration (default 180 s).
HomeNetworksHint: E.g. 192.168.1.0/24; separate several networks with commas. Outside these networks nothing is sent, not even through an externally reachable URL; Home Assistant sets Teams offline after its timeout. Empty = send everywhere.
AskForNewNetworks: Ask whether to add a new network
NewNetworkText:
The PC is in a new network: {0}

It is not in "Send only in these networks", so Teams Busy Light sends nothing here.

Yes: add the network, the status is sent here as well.
No: don't add it, don't ask again.
Cancel: stop asking about new networks (can be turned on in the settings).
Autostart: Start Teams Busy Light when I sign in to Windows
TestOk: Sent: {0}. Check the sensor in Home Assistant.
InvalidWebhook: Enter a valid HTTP or HTTPS webhook URL ending with /api/webhook/<id>.
InvalidNetwork: "{0}" is not a valid network. Enter networks like 192.168.1.0/24.
AlreadyRunning: Teams Busy Light is already running.
LogStarted: Teams Busy Light started on {0} for {1}
LogSendFailed: Failed to send status to Home Assistant: {0}
LogAway: Not in a home network, sending paused
LogHome: Back in a home network, sending again
LogNetworkAskOff: Asking about new networks turned off
MissingWebhook: No webhook URL configured. Open the settings of Teams Busy Light first.
InstallInfo: Teams Busy Light runs in the notification area for the signed-in Windows user and sends your Teams status to Home Assistant. No administrator rights are needed. Every Windows user installs it for themselves with their own integration entry and webhook URL.
InstallHosts: Add Home Assistant to the Windows hosts file (needs administrator rights)
InstallHostsHint: Only needed if Home Assistant cannot be reached by its name, e.g. while connected to a company VPN.
InstallLegacy: The previous Windows service "Microsoft Teams Status Monitor" will be removed (needs administrator rights). Other Windows users of this PC then have to install Teams Busy Light for themselves.
InstallComplete: Teams Busy Light is installed and running. You find it in the notification area of the taskbar (possibly behind the arrow) and in the Start menu.
AdminCancelled: The steps that need administrator rights were not run: {0}
AdminLegacy: removal of the previous Windows service
DnsFailed: IPv4 address for {0} could not be resolved using the DNS servers of active LAN/Wi-Fi adapters.
HostsFailed: Hosts file entry for '{0}' could not be updated: {1}
HostsRemoved: Hosts entries of Teams Busy Light removed.
LegacyRemoved: The previous Windows service and C:\Scripts\TeamsStatus were removed.
ServicePathMismatch: The service '{0}' does not appear to use the NSSM executable of the previous installation. It was not removed. Service path: {1}
ServiceRemovalFailed: The service '{0}' could not be removed (exit code {1}).
ServiceStillExists: The service '{0}' still exists after removal. The installed files were kept.
ConfirmUninstall: Remove Teams Busy Light for this Windows user? The Home Assistant integration entry is not changed.
UninstallHosts: Also remove the Teams Busy Light entries from the Windows hosts file (needs administrator rights)?
UninstallLegacy: The previous Windows service "Microsoft Teams Status Monitor" is still installed. Remove it as well (needs administrator rights)?
UninstallComplete: Teams Busy Light was removed. Home Assistant integration entries were not changed.
